output.brief:
The rise is mainly a technology fault, not a nursing-performance problem. When IT moved the alert relay server to new hardware on 12 August, the import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second wait for brief oxygen dips, suppression of repeat messages, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone. In Pods A–C, phone alerts per nurse per shift went from about 38 to about 82, acknowledgement time doubled, and incidents rose about fivefold. Pod D, still on the old server, did not change. Agency and core nurses have near-identical rates, and bedside alarm volume stayed flat, so staffing, acuity and the September monitor update do not explain it.

I'm about 90% sure of this cause.

Don't approve the agency cap or performance reviews, and don't switch off phone forwarding of oxygen alarms. Instead: re-import the missing rules (about 4 hours plus validation), get Clinical Engineering and alarm committee sign-off, hold Pod D's move until then, and track alerts per nurse and response times weekly.

Still open: possible wireless gaps (Room 14; logs show sending, not receipt) and whether the sick-leave rise is partly alarm-related (the virus season looks likelier).
